partners.mechanism_chain: ROBO1 (HGNC:10170) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal migration and axon guidance (GO:0007411); neuronal migration and axon guidance (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ congenital nystagmus (HP:0000744); HJV (HGNC:20870) —DISRUPTS→ hepcidin regulation (GO:0032931); hepcidin regulation (GO:0032931) —DECREASES→ hepcidin (UniProt:Q86Y47); hepcidin (UniProt:Q86Y47) —LEADS_TO→ hemochromatosis type 2A (MONDO:0011216). Loss-of-function mutations in ROBO1 disrupt neuronal migration and axon guidance, leading to congenital nystagmus. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in HJV disrupt hepcidin regulation, resulting in decreased hepcidin levels and iron overload characteristic of hemochromatosis type 2A. The shared module is the dysregulation of hepcidin, which, while primarily associated with iron homeostasis, can have broader cellular impacts. This hypothesis posits that altered iron homeostasis due to low hepcidin may indirectly affect neuronal function or development, contributing to or exacerbating nystagmus. Alternatively, both pathways could be influenced by a common upstream regulator or cellular process not explicitly detailed here.

#### 1. neurooculorenal syndrome  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.637)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373752, Reactome:R-HSA-376176, Reactome:R-HSA-428540, Reactome:R-HSA-428542, Reactome:R-HSA-8985801)

**Proposed mechanism:** ROBO1 loss-of-function variant (HGNC:10249) —DISRUPTS→ ROBO1 (HGNC:10249); ROBO1 (HGNC:10249) —DECREASES→ Slit-Robo signaling pathway (GO:0035607); Slit-Robo signaling pathway (GO:0035607) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal eye movement (nystagmus) (HP:0000506); Slit-Robo signaling pathway (GO:0035607) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal retinal morphology (HP:0030973); Slit-Robo signaling pathway (GO:0035607) —LEADS_TO→ Renal agenesis (HP:0000117). Loss-of-function variants in ROBO1 disrupt the Slit-Robo signaling pathway, which is crucial for proper neuronal guidance and development. Dysregulation of this pathway can lead to abnormal eye movements (nystagmus), abnormal retinal morphology, and renal developmental defects, explaining the shared and distinct phenotypes of the two diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in ROBO1 associated with a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease, or the complete absence of ROBO1 variants in well-characterized patients of either cohort, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs74815632)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ROBO1 in both congenital nystagmus and neurooculorenal syndrome could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at modulating the Slit-Robo signaling pathway to ameliorate ocular and renal manifestations.

**Why it matters:** Understanding this potential mechanistic link could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for congenital nystagmus by targeting iron metabolism pathways, or conversely, suggest monitoring for ocular abnormalities in patients with hemochromatosis type 2A.
